_about: Single source of truth for what the harness costs to enter. `ceilingBytes` is a ratchet frozen at the value measured when the budget was introduced: exceeding it fails the build. `targetBytes` is where the v3 redesign is heading; the report shows the gap. Lowering a ceiling is a deliberate act that belongs in the same commit as the pruning that earned it.
_accounting: A route's cost is everything the doctrine MANDATES reading before the first line of work, not only what the platform loads by default. That includes the frontmatter of every skill (permanently in context as `available_skills`) and any reference a head skill requires unconditionally. Counting only the default-loaded files is the measurement trap that made the 23/08 rollback attack the wrong target: the corpus on disk fell 8% while the per-turn cost stayed flat.

_skillLimits: Two kinds of rule. `spec` rules come from the published Agent Skills specification and from anthropics/skills quick_validate.py; they are hard errors because a violating skill can be rejected by the platform. `budget` rules are context-budget thresholds; they use a violation ratchet instead of a hard cap, because the v1 corpus already breaks them and a hard cap would block every commit while a bare warning would be ignored. `allowed` is frozen at today's count: introducing one more violation fails the build, and every slice of the v3 migration lowers the number in the commit that earned it.
_driftCheck: Every reference a head skill links to is either declared in the route that loads it, or listed under `onDemand` as consulted only inside a named branch. A link that appears in neither is drift: the doctrine grew a mandatory read that nobody budgeted.
